metadata.source_policy: Links checked for core event and timing only; source independence and image rights stored separately.
metadata.note: All previously weak Tier 3 primaries now replaced at core-event/date research level. No independent verification of alternate stories was added. Same-institution/derived data are explicitly distinguished from independent measurements.

cases.title: The Great Blizzard of 1978 reaches Ohio and the Great Lakes
cases.primary_angle: Explain how explosive cyclone deepening and Arctic air created near-total transport paralysis.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare observed pressure and winds with 1978 warning bulletins; distinguish land observations from the storm central pressure.
cases.verified_core_fact: On January 26, 1978 a rapidly deepening storm brought destructive blizzard conditions to Ohio and surrounding Great Lakes states.
cases.graphic_type: Meteorological analysis
cases.graphic_data_source_note: U.S. NWS storm maps, archived surface analyses and original warning texts; use specific observation locations and timestamps.
cases.research_note: Duration Jan 25–27; no single-day totals as full-storm totals; NWS studies within NOAA are not institutionally independent.

cases.title: The mysterious 1884 Enigma tornado outbreak
cases.primary_angle: Why a devastating 1884 outbreak remains difficult to reconstruct despite early attempts at tornado forecasting.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain how John Park Finley's contemporary observations shaped early tornado forecasting without claiming a precise modern outbreak count.
cases.verified_core_fact: The Enigma tornado outbreak began February 19, 1884, affecting the U.S. Southeast; historical documentation cannot conclusively establish the number of tornadoes.
cases.graphic_type: Historical event map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NOAA Heritage includes a specific Finley historical tornado map credited Public Domain; do not imply exact modern tracks.
cases.research_note: Both sources within NOAA/NWS; 19–20 Feb outbreak, counts disputed. NOAA Heritage specifically labels the Finley map public domain, not necessarily other assets.

cases.title: Gainesville's catastrophic 1936 tornado
cases.source_publisher: Digital Library of Georgia / Georgia Archives
cases.primary_angle: Use original documented Gainesville streetscape damage rather than an uncertain single tornado-path reconstruction.
cases.alternate_angle: Explore visibility and urban vulnerability using dated photographs; do not conflate Tupelo's April 5 toll with Gainesville's April 6 toll.
cases.verified_core_fact: A destructive tornado struck Gainesville, Georgia on April 6, 1936, documented in contemporary Georgia archival photography.
cases.graphic_type: Historical photograph with contextual annotations
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Georgia Archives original dated photographs and city streets; individual photograph licensing must be checked.
cases.research_note: NWS biographical page gives potentially inaccurate specific school casualty figures; do NOT reuse those statistics. Verify individual photo rights with Georgia Archives.

cases.title: The deadly 1953 Waco downtown tornado
cases.primary_angle: Investigate how heavy rain limited visibility and why the Waco catastrophe helped spur advances in tornado warnings.
cases.alternate_angle: Contrast the historic city damage footprint and 1953 warning process using original mapped records.
cases.verified_core_fact: An F5 tornado devastated central Waco on May 11, 1953; NWS reports 114 deaths and 597 injuries attributable to this tornado.
cases.graphic_type: Historical event map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS city map and Waco city historic aerial/street map; NWS page's Tribune-Herald photographs are explicitly copyrighted.
cases.research_note: City history cites NOAA as a source, so it is not fully independent factual corroboration; archival photos on NWS page credit Waco Tribune-Herald, do not reuse absent permission.

cases.title: The weather window behind the D-Day invasion
cases.primary_angle: Compare competing wartime forecast methods and explain why 6 June was judged marginally workable.
cases.alternate_angle: Show authenticated Allied versus German synoptic charts, noting unequal observational access and analysis times.
cases.verified_core_fact: The invasion of Normandy began June 6, 1944 after forecast conditions prompted postponement from June 5; the Met Office identifies a marginal but usable weather window.
cases.graphic_type: Meteorological analysis
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Met Office National Meteorological Archive originals; Met Office source material cites Crown Copyright/Open Government Licence; German DWD charts require separate permission.
cases.research_note: The invasion itself is historical context; meteorological story is forecast uncertainty and narrow weather window. Do not assume German charts are covered by the Met Office OGL.

cases.title: Pine Lake campground tornado in Alberta
cases.primary_angle: A Canadian severe-weather anniversary: show the preconvective enhanced-V satellite signature and real local storm progression.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain why satellite observation times fall on July 15 UTC while the tornado occurred July 14 MDT.
cases.verified_core_fact: A destructive tornado struck Pine Lake, Alberta on July 14, 2000 local time; Public Safety Canada records 12 fatalities.
cases.graphic_type: Observational chart
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Authentic NOAA GOES-8/10 and NOAA-12 observations published by UW–Madison CIMSS; determine rights for the particular image, not the satellite platform.
cases.research_note: Canadian disaster database says >140 injured, CIMSS >100; do not quote precise injuries without reconciliation. CIMSS local date July 14 / UTC July 15.

cases.title: Ellicott City's devastating 2016 flash flood
cases.primary_angle: Explain how nearly stationary heavy-rain cells and narrow urban drainage produced rapid flooding.
cases.alternate_angle: Build a real-time warning–rainfall–flooding timeline from the NWS case study and gauge-based USGS research.
cases.verified_core_fact: An intense rainfall episode caused severe flash flooding in historic Ellicott City on July 30, 2016; NWS reports two fatalities.
cases.graphic_type: Timeline
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS local rain gauge and MRMS estimation, USGS hydrology; distinguish estimates, gauges and source copyright.
cases.research_note: This is an upgrade of an existing NCEI Ellicott City lead, not a different occurrence. Do not confuse with the May 27, 2018 flood; keep previous event ID as linked source segment.

cases.title: Hurricane Katrina makes its northern Gulf Coast landfalls
cases.primary_angle: Focus on the distinction between landfall-category winds, the expansive wind field and storm-surge footprint.
cases.alternate_angle: Create a sourced track-and-surge graphic separating Louisiana and Mississippi coastline impacts.
cases.verified_core_fact: Katrina made landfall along the northern Gulf Coast on August 29, 2005, bringing widespread wind and devastating storm surge.
cases.graphic_type: Storm track or tornado path
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NHC HURDAT2 best track and official TCR; NWS Mobile observed surge data; request individual original photographs if desired.
cases.research_note: NHC and NWS both NOAA: corroborating documents but not institutionally independent. Avoid conflating peak Category 5 Gulf intensity with Category 3 at landfall; distinguish landfalls.

cases.title: The Great Miami Hurricane of 1926
cases.primary_angle: Follow the 35-minute eye lull and how people mistook temporary calm for the end of the storm.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare original Weather Bureau observer notes with modern timing and forecast methods without invented wind readings.
cases.verified_core_fact: The Great Miami Hurricane struck South Florida early September 18, 1926, when short-lead warnings and unfamiliarity with hurricanes worsened its impacts.
cases.graphic_type: Timeline
cases.graphic_data_source_note: 1926 U.S. Weather Bureau original record and Florida Memory archival collections; photo-specific rights unreviewed.
cases.research_note: Both core sources are within NOAA. Beware differing quoted mortality totals (Miami-area vs full hurricane), later reconstruction of winds and modernized landfall location.

cases.title: The 1927 St. Louis tornado through the city center
cases.primary_angle: Follow the tornado's route through a dense city using period street addresses and photos.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain how contemporary sources differ on casualty totals and how early observational limitations affect estimated intensity.
cases.verified_core_fact: A violent tornado struck central St. Louis on September 29, 1927, leaving extensive damage documented by period photography.
cases.graphic_type: Historical event map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: St. Louis Public Library tornado photo collection and historic street maps; each photo rights status must be checked.
cases.research_note: NWS St. Louis lists 72 deaths, St. Louis Public Library 78, Missouri emergency management 79. Do not publish exact casualty figure before reconciliation. Pre-1970 Fujita ratings are retrospective, not original EF ratings.

cases.title: The Pacific Northwest Columbus Day windstorm
cases.primary_angle: Trace how a powerful extratropical storm generated destructive winds well inland and across the region.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare authentic historic wind observations and the cyclone track without conflating 12–13 October local dates.
cases.verified_core_fact: A historically significant windstorm struck the Pacific Northwest on October 12, 1962.
cases.graphic_type: Historical event map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NOAA archived surface maps, state observatory wind records and documented historical maps; asset rights pending.
cases.research_note: NWS Aberdeen page reproduces externally sourced weather-history graphics, do not assume its images are public domain; check location of peak readings.

cases.title: The record-deep Upper Midwest cyclone of 2010
cases.primary_angle: Explore how a rapidly deepening inland cyclone produced strong winds, tornadoes, blizzard conditions and extreme pressure observations.
cases.alternate_angle: Show Bigfork's measured/derived pressure time series against historically documented inland minima.
cases.verified_core_fact: Bigfork, Minnesota registered a computed sea-level pressure of 955.2 hPa on October 26, 2010 during a powerful extratropical cyclone.
cases.graphic_type: Observational chart
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS Duluth source shows station data and pressure graphs; use calculations with station, time and units, not a nationwide record claim.
cases.research_note: NWS explicitly states 955.2 hPa was NOT the lowest pressure ever in CONUS; AWOS sea-level pressure derived from station pressure, and coastal records lower. Avoid misleading all-time US record headlines.

cases.title: The great Florence flood on the Arno River
cases.primary_angle: Tell the meteorological-to-hydrological sequence behind a flood that endangered centuries of cultural heritage.
cases.alternate_angle: Map the Arno flood timeline with authentic high-water marks and documented archival images.
cases.verified_core_fact: After prolonged rain, the Arno overflowed into Florence on November 4, 1966, inundating historic neighborhoods, libraries and artwork.
cases.graphic_type: Historical event map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Italian Civil Protection high-water marker documentation; National Library flood photograph collection and archived records; copyrights unreviewed.
cases.research_note: Italian Civil Protection page lists 35 victims in region; National Central Library says 39. Do not publish a fatality count without scope reconciliation; dated 3–4 Nov overnight.

cases.title: The catastrophic 1977 Andhra Pradesh cyclone
cases.secondary_source_publisher: Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority
cases.primary_angle: Use original Madras cyclone-radar study to show its double-eyewall structure and near-coastal evolution.
cases.alternate_angle: Discuss how observing limitations affected coastal-track and cyclone-intensity interpretation.
cases.verified_core_fact: An intense Bay of Bengal cyclone hit the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 19, 1977, documented by contemporary cyclone-warning radar.
cases.graphic_type: Meteorological analysis
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Original IMD radar-study paper charts and state archival cyclone track; article licensing statements conflict and commercial reuse needs checking.
cases.research_note: IMD and Andhra state sources agree broadly on Nov 19 coastal strike, but accounts differ on precise landfall locality (Nizampatnam, Chirala, Bapatla). Do not state exact location, deaths, or max winds as settled.

cases.title: The violent gale and Tay Bridge collapse of 1879
cases.primary_angle: Explain the wind-loading meteorology of the 1879 storm, grounded in contemporary records rather than dramatized artwork.
cases.alternate_angle: Contrast original wind observations, inquiry documents and later wind engineering lessons, carefully separating causes from atmospheric conditions.
cases.verified_core_fact: A violent gale struck Scotland on December 28, 1879, as the Tay Rail Bridge collapsed while a train crossed.
cases.graphic_type: Historical photograph with contextual annotations
cases.graphic_data_source_note: National Records of Scotland inquiry records, archival bridge plans, historical barometric analyses; individual image rights pending.
cases.research_note: National Records say 59 known passengers/victims versus inquiry estimate ~74–75 aboard; other histories quote ~75. Do not assert the precise death count or wind alone as sole engineering cause.

cases.title: The Burns' Day Storm brings damaging daytime winds to Britain
cases.primary_angle: Show how a rapidly moving extratropical cyclone produced severe daytime gusts across a heavily populated region; explain why timing mattered.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare the Met Office's 12 UTC synoptic analysis and observed gust distribution with the 1987 storm, using consistent wind measures.
cases.verified_core_fact: On 25 January 1990 an intense extratropical depression tracked across southern Scotland and brought severe daytime winds to England and Wales.
cases.graphic_type: Station wind gust map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Met Office document provides a 12 UTC analysis and station gust chart; verify underlying data availability and reuse terms before redrawing.
cases.research_note: Royal Meteorological Society and Met Office are distinct organizations, but the Society cites Met Office wind data; do not call measurement evidence independent. 47 reported deaths and 93 kt maximum gust are source claims pending claim-level review. Historic chart and photos not asset-cleared.

cases.title: The 2003 Presidents' Day snowstorm reaches the Mid-Atlantic
cases.location: Central Pennsylvania and Washington metropolitan area
cases.primary_angle: Show how the storm spread a wide swath of heavy snow across the Mid-Atlantic, with multi-day snowfall totals clearly dated.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare 16–18 February snowfall gradients and snow-versus-sleet differences in central Pennsylvania and the Washington area.
cases.verified_core_fact: By 16 February 2003 a major snowstorm was affecting central Pennsylvania and the Washington region; snow persisted in parts of the region through 18 February.
cases.graphic_type: Observed snowfall map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS State College maps co-op/spotter totals through 17 February; obtain station-by-station totals and timeframe before original mapping.
cases.research_note: This is a multi-day 16–18 February event, not a one-day snowfall record. The Washington Post article provides contemporary independent reporting for the DC region, not a full-storm independent meteorological analysis. NWS page reports 12–30 inch regional snowfall but any numeric claim needs station and time-window verification. Rights of photographs not checked.

cases.title: The 1965 Palm Sunday tornado outbreak strikes the Great Lakes
cases.location: Indiana and neighboring Great Lakes states
cases.secondary_source_publisher: Wells County Historical Society and Museum
cases.primary_angle: Explain why tornadoes spread across several states and how the warning-to-public communication chain worked in 1965.
cases.alternate_angle: Use a new, sourced tornado-path schematic to describe the unusual near-simultaneous tornadoes without republishing copyrighted news photographs.
cases.verified_core_fact: On 11 April 1965 multiple destructive tornadoes struck Indiana and other Midwestern/Great Lakes states during the Palm Sunday outbreak.
cases.graphic_type: Historical tornado-track reconstruction
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Use official storm-track data and original geographic rendering; famous Paul Huffman twin-tornado and press photos have distinct copyright ownership and are NOT cleared.
cases.research_note: NWS Indianapolis and Wells County Historical Society support event/date/Indiana impacts. Published outbreak-wide death counts differ between NWS summaries (e.g. 260 vs 271); do not include totals without defining source, time frame and tornado scope. Historic photos are not cleared for reuse. 1965 warning methods must be independently and accurately characterized.

cases.title: Paris halts navigation as the 1910 Seine flood builds
cases.primary_angle: Explain why months of wet weather and saturated soils primed the Seine basin, and why river navigation halted on 20 January before the later crest.
cases.alternate_angle: Trace how floodwaters spread into Paris via surface streets, transit infrastructure and underground passages rather than claiming a single sudden river-wall failure.
cases.verified_core_fact: On 20 January 1910, Paris suspended navigation on the rising Seine because boats could no longer pass under bridges; the broader flood developed over multiple days.
cases.graphic_type: Historic river-stage timeline with city river map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Search French hydrometric archives and chart dated stage observations for the Seine; archival postcards/photos have separate ownership and reuse conditions.
cases.research_note: This anniversary is the 20 January navigation suspension, NOT the 1910 Seine flood crest (28 January). Cumulative rain Jan 15–20, and saturated soils from 1909, are documented; no crest-height figure validated. French archive images and postal cards are not cleared for reuse.

cases.title: The Buffalo Blizzard of 1977 begins amid deep pre-existing snow
cases.secondary_source_publisher: Northeast Regional Climate Center, Cornell University
cases.primary_angle: Explain how powerful wind mobilized snow already on the ground and the frozen Lake Erie ice surface, making snow transport—not just new accumulation—the defining hazard.
cases.alternate_angle: Reconstruct the chronology of the wind shift, whiteout and ground blizzard using hourly meteorological observations; compare visibility against new snow.
cases.verified_core_fact: The Blizzard of 1977 began in western New York on 28 January 1977 and continued into early February, with deep pre-existing snow helping produce severe blowing snow.
cases.graphic_type: Historical observation timeline and Lake Erie ice map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS Buffalo chronology and Cornell/NRCC Great Lakes ice-cover reference; create original georeferenced schematic from observation data rather than reusing uncertain-license photographs.
cases.research_note: NWS says snowfall commenced near 5 a.m. Jan 28 on top of pre-existing 37-inch snowpack; avoid implying zero new snowfall or treating windblown snow as all fresh. Cornell NRCC may rely on NOAA observations, so not independent measurements. The 1887 giant-snowflake lead for this date remains held, NOT selected due to disputed reporting date.

cases.title: The February 2013 Northeast blizzard begins
cases.location: Boston, southern New England and Long Island
cases.primary_angle: Explain the coastal-low evolution and mesoscale snow bands, while carefully distinguishing the Feb 8 onset from Feb 9 storm totals.
cases.alternate_angle: Map observed Long Island/Connecticut snowfall maxima alongside pressure and wind observations, drawing on timestamped reports rather than preliminary forecast graphics.
cases.verified_core_fact: On 8 February 2013 a major nor'easter brought worsening snow and wind to southern New England and the New York area; its heaviest accumulations continued into 9 February.
cases.graphic_type: Original storm-total snowfall/pressure analysis
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS storm report lists observed station/spotter snowfall with timestamps; map station reports after checking quality and accumulation windows.
cases.research_note: WBUR aired contemporaneous coverage on Feb 8; NWS tabulates accumulations ending Feb 9. Do not attribute multi-day totals to Feb 8 alone. Review discrepancies between spotter, official airport, and preliminary reports. WBUR/AP/NOAA illustrative photos are NOT reuse-cleared.

cases.title: Extreme rainfall intensifies on Australia's New South Wales Mid North Coast
cases.location: Mid North Coast of New South Wales
cases.secondary_source_publisher: New South Wales Department of Primary Industries
cases.primary_angle: Show how persistent moist easterly flow into eastern New South Wales and a coastal low brought intense rainfall starting 19 March, leading to catastrophic flooding later in the event.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain the role of a blocked synoptic pattern and saturated soils; contrast rainfall timing across the Mid North Coast versus Sydney later in the week.
cases.verified_core_fact: A major multiday rainfall and flood event affected eastern New South Wales in March 2021; the Australian Bureau of Meteorology places the start of the heaviest Mid North Coast rain on 19 March.
cases.graphic_type: Daily rainfall sequence and pressure-pattern map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Bureau of Meteorology Special Climate Statement 74 has dated rain panels and daily synoptic analyses; check map-data reproduction terms and measurements before preparing new map.
cases.research_note: BOM Special Climate Statement 74 says coastal rain began March 17–18 and heaviest rain started March 19 Mid North Coast; highest rainfall and flooding elsewhere occurred later. NSW state analysis corroborates March event but not necessarily the exact first day; it uses BOM observations. BOM original PDF screenshot retrieval was unavailable; precise day supported by published text extracted by the search tool. No rainfall totals or rights approved.

cases.title: The Memorial Day flash flood begins on the Blanco River at Wimberley
cases.location: Wimberley and Blanco River, Texas Hill Country
cases.secondary_source_publisher: USGS flood response and streamgage records
cases.primary_angle: Show the extraordinary river-stage acceleration late on 23 May using the NWS warning and gauge timeline, without mislabeling the 24 May crest as a 23 May reading.
cases.alternate_angle: Analyze terrain, intense upstream rainfall and rapidly changing flash-flood response; distinguish estimated peak from recorder readings after gauge damage.
cases.verified_core_fact: Flash flooding developed along the Blanco River near Wimberley late on 23 May 2015; the river rose rapidly and reached extreme levels early on 24 May.
cases.graphic_type: Custom hydrograph and warning timeline
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS Austin/San Antonio hydrologic chronology shows station stage and flash flood emergency issuance; confirm time zone, gauge censoring and reproduction rights before redrawing.
cases.research_note: NWS document ties late-23rd warnings to extraordinary stage rises overnight into May 24; USGS documents the broader 2015 flood and instrument damage. Never call 40.21 ft a 23 May peak: highest stage was reported 01:00 on May 24, and values/metadata should be inspected prior to tweeting. Do not infer all floodwaters were measured after station failure. Historic photos not cleared.

cases.title: Category 5 Hurricane Irma crosses Barbuda and the northern Leeward Islands
cases.location: Barbuda, Saint Martin and northern Leeward Islands
cases.primary_angle: Track Irma across the northern Leewards and explain why islands near the path experienced dramatically different wind and storm-surge exposure.
cases.alternate_angle: Contrast contemporaneous island-level CDEMA situation reports with best-track estimated winds and separately measured observations.
cases.verified_core_fact: During the early hours of 6 September 2017, Category 5 Hurricane Irma struck Barbuda and Saint Martin and severely affected the northern Leeward Islands.
cases.graphic_type: Hurricane track, islands and observation markers
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Use original track plotting from official NHC best-track tables and geospatial island boundaries; satellite imagery subject to asset-specific terms.
cases.research_note: CDEMA initial SitRep on September 6 reports Barbuda radio loss and damage. Do not use CDEMA early impact tallies as final. 185 mph is storm maximum intensity, not necessarily directly observed at every island. NWS description says 'northern Leeward Islands'; verify precise center path and local dates against final NHC TCR before drafting.

cases.title: Record floods and streamflow peaks spread along Colorado's Front Range
cases.location: Boulder and northern Front Range, Colorado
cases.primary_angle: Use specific Boulder-area gauge records to show why the flood became severe by 12–13 September, separating runoff timing from precipitation totals.
cases.alternate_angle: Map how orographic lift, a persistent moist feed and saturated basins drove geographically uneven river and debris-flow response.
cases.verified_core_fact: Major flooding affected Colorado's northern Front Range in September 2013, with the U.S. Geological Survey documenting many flood-peak streamflows on 12 or 13 September.
cases.graphic_type: Observed streamgage peak timing map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: USGS streamgage sites and time series can support a new map; avoid incorrectly treating reach-level inferred peaks as directly instrument-measured.
cases.research_note: USGS flood-peak timing is mostly Sep 12–13, not all Sep 13; City of Boulder dates broader event Sep 11–15. Do not describe September 13 as the single onset or storm-total precipitation day. Separate USGS inferred values from measured stage; retain station identifiers, rating-curve limitations and gauge period of record.

cases.title: A powerful atmospheric river reaches British Columbia
cases.location: South coast and Fraser Valley, British Columbia
cases.primary_angle: Explain how an atmospheric-river moisture corridor met already saturated terrain, turning the 13–15 November rain event into destructive flooding and infrastructure failures.
cases.alternate_angle: Use a public-source moisture transport map and a dated three-day rainfall sequence to explain mountain enhancement and the river response.
cases.verified_core_fact: Environment and Climate Change Canada dates the arrival of a major atmospheric river on the British Columbia coast to 13 November 2021; intense rain and flooding followed during 13–15 November.
cases.graphic_type: Atmospheric moisture plume and rainfall timeline
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NASA Earth Observatory satellite and rainfall context; identify exact data and media licensing before reuse, including any third-party imagery credits.
cases.research_note: ECCC states storm arrived November 13; Public Safety Canada alternatively describes significant rainfall as beginning November 14. Frame 13 as storm arrival, not first major inundation, and distinguish multiple November atmospheric rivers from the 13–15 episode. NASA independently describes the Nov13–15 moisture event, may cite shared meteorological datasets. Impacts figures subject to evolving assessments.

cases.title: Hail and heavy rain disable Southern Airways Flight 242's engines
cases.primary_angle: Show how intense hail and precipitation ingestion and aviation-weather communication limitations contributed to a loss of thrust in both engines.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain the gap between onboard airborne-radar interpretation, route-level convective weather, and timely dispatch/ATC hazards without overstating radar capabilities.
cases.verified_core_fact: On April 4, 1977, Southern Airways Flight 242 encountered a severe thunderstorm near Rome, Georgia; heavy hail and water ingestion contributed to loss of thrust and a fatal forced landing at New Hope.
cases.graphic_type: Original convective weather/flight-route chronology
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NTSB report includes flight chronology and discussions of onboard radar; design an original schematic with clearly labeled uncertainty, not a copied cockpit map or accident photo.
cases.research_note: FAA retells NTSB findings, not an independent causal investigation. Do not claim hail alone mechanically caused the loss of power; NTSB identifies rain/hail ingestion together with thrust lever movements and compressor damage. Historic images/accident material rights pending. NTSB report p. 2 was visually checked.

cases.title: The May 8, 2009 Super Derecho crosses the central United States
cases.location: Southeast Kansas, Missouri Ozarks and southern Illinois
cases.primary_angle: Trace how a long-lived bow echo and mesoscale circulation drove destructive straight-line winds across state boundaries.
cases.alternate_angle: Build a radar/verified wind-report timeline using available imagery and measured gusts, separating derecho winds from tornado damage.
cases.verified_core_fact: A long-lived derecho produced widespread damaging winds on May 8, 2009 across southeast Kansas, southern Missouri and adjoining states.
cases.graphic_type: Custom derecho track and radar-timeline map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS Springfield storm tracks and wind reports; confirm station timestamps, radar availability and licensing before preparing unique graphics.
cases.research_note: Both named sources are NWS offices within NOAA; not independent organizations. Peer-reviewed research ('The 8 May 2009 Superderecho: Analysis of a Real-Time Explicit Convective Forecast') can inform future claim-level dynamics, but full paper was not read in this pass. Do not attribute tornado damage to straight-line winds.

cases.title: An F3 tornado cuts through downtown Kalamazoo, Michigan
cases.primary_angle: Reconstruct the short, unusually urban tornado corridor and explain why precise street-level historical track mapping differs from broad county tornado catalogs.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare original damage maps with historical city streets without reusing copyrighted newspaper photographs.
cases.verified_core_fact: On May 13, 1980, an F3 tornado struck Kalamazoo, Michigan, leaving an approximately 11-mile damage path through the city.
cases.graphic_type: Original historic-city tornado path map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Museum exhibit supplies original oral histories, photographs, damage documentation; license/permissions are separate for each asset, so map from independently verified survey geography.
cases.research_note: Museum lists 16-minute path, 5 killed and 79 seriously hurt, but casualty classifications and full track locations need claim-level verification before captions. NWS GRR links to an external ArcGIS story map; not necessarily independent of the museum source. Historic press photos have explicit copyright.

cases.title: Exceptional rain triggers flash flooding around Krymsk, Russia
cases.primary_angle: Explain how intense rainfall in the Caucasus foothills generated rapid runoff toward the lower-lying city of Krymsk.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare a dated July 7 flood-context image with later July 10 ISS imagery without passing off post-event scars as live flooding.
cases.verified_core_fact: Severe rain and flash flooding struck Krymsk and its surroundings on July 7–8, 2012; NASA and WHO document the event and affected area.
cases.graphic_type: Caucasus basin terrain and flood-footprint comparison
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NASA article distinguishes July 7 aerial flood image from July 10 ISS post-flood photo; assess source/asset rights, credits, georeferencing and date before any actual reuse.
cases.research_note: NASA's storm total more than 30 cm is second-hand; check gauge times/quality before publication. WHO confirms flood 7–8 July and aftermath, NOT rainfall measurements. WHO images carry copyright © WHO and require permissions; treat as unlicensed. Do not quote a death count from early reports as a final figure.

cases.title: An extraordinary early-season Montana snowstorm draws to a close
cases.primary_angle: Explain how moist upslope northeasterly flow and strong cold advection supported heavy September snow while many trees still carried leaves.
cases.alternate_angle: Contrast observed two-day Great Falls snowfall with typical September snowfall and show how regional snow bands differed from mountain peaks.
cases.verified_core_fact: An unusually heavy early-season snowstorm affected Montana during September 28–30, 2019, with extensive snow cover visible in satellite imagery on October 1.
cases.graphic_type: Original snow-cover satellite analysis and station totals
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NASA Terra MODIS false-color imagery was acquired October 1, one day AFTER September 30 anniversary; annotate acquisition date prominently and verify NASA image/third-party data reuse.
cases.research_note: Sept30 marks the late-stage multi-day snowstorm; Great Falls 19.3 in was a TWO-day total, not a Sept30 single-day snow total; verify final official station observation before caption. NPR relies on NWS observational reports. Photos/NASA composite layer terms pending.

cases.title: Storm Alex drives extreme Alpine rain and devastating floods in France
cases.primary_angle: Explain how a jet-driven low and southward moisture flux created orographically enhanced, extraordinary rainfall in the Maritime Alps.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare valley-specific measured 24-hour rainfall and downstream flood impacts, distinguishing station records from unmeasured river peaks.
cases.verified_core_fact: On October 2, 2020, Storm Alex helped drive extreme rainfall over the Alpes-Maritimes in southeastern France, triggering destructive floods.
cases.graphic_type: Topographic rainfall and moisture-flow map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Météo-France lists station rainfall in 24 hours and synoptic dynamics; digitize observation values and make a newly sourced map only after validating timestamps, metadata, rights.
cases.research_note: Météo-France reports 500 mm at Saint-Martin-Vésubie in 24h, but final post needs station identifier and time window. Alex also caused severe wind in Brittany and subsequent rain in neighboring countries; do not conflate wind maxima with the Alps floods. Copernicus may reuse Météo-France observations. Media-rights pending.

cases.title: Hurricane Wilma deepens to a record 882 mb over the Caribbean
cases.location: Northwestern Caribbean Sea, east of Yucatán Peninsula
cases.primary_angle: Reconstruct Wilma's extraordinary rapid intensification and tight inner core from best-track estimates and aircraft recon evidence.
cases.alternate_angle: Plot the pressure fall against hurricane center position and wind changes, distinguishing estimated best-track minimum from direct aircraft observations.
cases.verified_core_fact: On October 19, 2005, Hurricane Wilma intensified to a minimum best-track central pressure of 882 mb in the northwestern Caribbean, the lowest documented for an Atlantic hurricane.
cases.graphic_type: Best-track pressure and intensity time-series
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Reconstruct observations from HURDAT2 and NHC best-track rather than copying TCR maps; check UTC/local date and whether 882 mb is analyzed vs directly observed.
cases.research_note: NHC best track shows 882 mb at 1200 UTC Oct19; other NOAA prose quotes around 0800 UTC minimum or aircraft observed pressure. Distinguish best-track timing from instantaneous aircraft measurements. The Oct19 anniversary is peak intensity NOT Florida landfall (Oct24). NHC/WPC same NOAA.

cases.title: Diablo winds fuel the Oakland Hills firestorm
cases.source_publisher: Oakland Public Library / Oakland History Center
cases.primary_angle: Explain how dry easterly downslope Diablo winds rapidly transformed smoldering vegetation into an explosive urban-wildland firestorm.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare contemporary NWS Red Flag messaging, synoptic pressure gradients and terrain-aligned fire spread without claiming the wind alone caused each ignition.
cases.verified_core_fact: On the morning of October 20, 1991, strong easterly winds reignited a small fire in the Oakland hills and rapidly spread a devastating firestorm.
cases.graphic_type: Topographic wind-flow and observed fire progression
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Recreate a terrain, wind and ignition schematic using independently sourced geographic data and time stamps; Oakland Library archival photographs require separate permission.
cases.research_note: Oakland Public Library describes prior fire October 19 and winds/reignition October 20; do NOT date initial ignition on October 20. EBRPD page has erroneous 'Sunday Oct. 21' text and is not used for date corroboration. The research paper models 1991 atmospheric dynamics; it does not prove the cause of each spot fire. Avoid media injury/death counts until independently reconciled.

cases.title: The Great Storm of 1703 devastates southern Britain
cases.location: Southern England, the Thames estuary and English Channel
cases.primary_angle: Tell the story through contemporaneous barometer observations and documented shipping losses while openly explaining the 11-day calendar change.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain how Defoe's 1704 account helped preserve pre-instrumental-era weather observations, with a historically accurate Julian-to-Gregorian date panel.
cases.verified_core_fact: The Great Storm struck southern England on 26 November 1703 in the Julian calendar used there at the time, equivalent to 7 December 1703 in the modern Gregorian calendar.
cases.graphic_type: Historic source excerpts and Julian/Gregorian timeline
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Research original Defoe 1704 text and archival scans, with item-level image and text rights checks. Make a newly designed calendar conversion diagram, not fabricated historical wind contour data.
cases.research_note: The storm continued 7–8 December Gregorian; contemporary sources usually say Nov26–27 OLD STYLE. Avoid claiming 120 mph as a modern anemometer reading; historic reports and reconstructed pressure/wind values vary. Never present historic death and ships lost estimates without scope and source. University York explicitly footnotes Dec7 Gregorian.

cases.title: An intense snowband leaves Binghamton with 40 inches of snow
cases.location: Binghamton and New York Southern Tier
cases.primary_angle: Explain the mesoscale snowband, snow-to-liquid ratio and unusually high hourly snowfall rates along the inland nor'easter track.
cases.alternate_angle: Plot verified Binghamton airport snowfall and radar evolution without blending nearby 44-inch community spotter totals with official airport measurements.
cases.verified_core_fact: During December 16–17, 2020, a nor'easter produced exceptional banded snowfall across the Northeast; a two-day total of 40 inches was recorded at Greater Binghamton Airport.
cases.graphic_type: Radar band evolution and official two-day snowfall chart
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Use NWS radar replay and official climate record through December 17, clearly labeling 40 in as two-day storm total, not 24-h or Dec17-only.
cases.research_note: NWS BGM report and Cornell climate summary refer to common NOAA station/spotter observation networks; both support storm period but NOT two independent gauges. WPC preliminary state 24-hour snow records need SCEC review; avoid those claims. Original radar products and photographic license pending.

cases.title: The December 2006 blizzard shuts down Denver-area travel
cases.primary_angle: Explain front-range upslope snow development and the aviation/travel consequences of a major December 20–21 snowstorm.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare Denver's verified storm total and terrain-controlled suburban/foothills accumulations; avoid using isolated mountain maxima as city totals.
cases.verified_core_fact: A major blizzard began in the Denver area on December 20, 2006, continuing into December 21 and causing widespread travel disruption.
cases.graphic_type: Denver-area snowfall gradient map and travel timeline
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NASA post-storm imagery supports a snow-cover map but is not a December 20 in-storm observation; combine independently sourced NWS station snowfall with exact timing.
cases.research_note: NWS Denver/Boulder documents a 20–21 December snowstorm nearly 2 feet; 20.7-inch storm total appears in NWS climate summaries and should not be labeled 20 Dec alone. The adjacent Dec18 cold and Dec19 snow primaries create a winter-hazard repetition warning; flag for subsequent swap/reorder. NASA/NOAA share basic observation networks.

cases.title: Smokehouse Creek Fire ignites during a Texas Panhandle fire-weather outbreak
cases.location: Texas Panhandle near Stinnett, Hutchinson County
cases.primary_angle: Explain how very dry grasses, anomalous warmth and strong downslope/synoptic winds drove extraordinary fire spread during February 26–27.
cases.alternate_angle: Map the progression of satellite thermal anomalies and observed wind speeds, distinguishing the ignition time from the later acreage maximum.
cases.verified_core_fact: The Smokehouse Creek Fire began in the Texas Panhandle on February 26, 2024, during a major wind-driven wildfire outbreak.
cases.graphic_type: Timestamped fire spread and wind observations
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS meteorological analysis and NASA MODIS imagery from Feb 27, not from ignition itself; the image's acquisition date and item-level rights must be validated.
cases.research_note: NOAA/NCEI reports a damaged power pole as an ignition source, but the physical cause was initially unknown in contemporaneous NASA text. Do not describe causation as established without checking final fire-investigation records. Over 1 million acres is total fire footprint after multiple days, NOT an amount burned on Feb 26. NASA satellite from Feb 27 must not be labeled Feb 26.

cases.title: Historic eastern Kentucky floodwaters continue downstream as gauges fail
cases.location: Whitesburg, Hazard and eastern Kentucky river basins
cases.primary_angle: Follow the July 29 downstream crest response after catastrophic overnight July 27–28 rainfall, showing why some river gauges were overtopped or destroyed.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain how training thunderstorms over steep watersheds produced record streamflow and why indirect post-flood measurements may differ from the last logged gage value.
cases.verified_core_fact: On July 29, 2022, USGS field crews were tracking downstream flood crests and damaged streamgages after devastating flooding in eastern Kentucky.
cases.graphic_type: Hydrograph and damaged-gage response timeline
cases.graphic_data_source_note: The dated July 29 USGS response bulletin identifies broken gauges and downstream crest monitoring; build an original schematic from time-stamped gage records only after verification.
cases.research_note: Most intense rainfall was July 27–28, not July 29. Whitesburg gauge was reportedly destroyed after surpassing a prior record; do not present the final inferred crest as a direct continuous instrument reading. USGS and NWS observations overlap but independently describe response and meteorological onset.

cases.title: Category 4 Hurricane Harvey makes landfall near Rockport, Texas
cases.location: San José Island and Rockport, Texas coast
cases.primary_angle: Contrast Harvey's rapid approach and coastal Category 4 wind/surge hazard on August 25 with the multiday catastrophic inland rainfall that followed.
cases.alternate_angle: Reconstruct the storm-center track against 25 August GOES imagery, showing how storm translation slowed only later as heavy rain shifted inland.
cases.verified_core_fact: Harvey made landfall along the central Texas coast around 10 p.m. CDT on August 25, 2017 as a Category 4 hurricane.
cases.graphic_type: Original landfall track and satellite chronology
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS historical radar/satellite, NASA acquisition and NHC best-track data; check final best-track fixes and specific satellite source/image credits before use.
cases.research_note: August 25 is Harvey's Texas landfall anniversary, not the later Houston rainfall peak. NWS offices may use San José Island, Port Aransas, or Rockport as geographic shorthand; use the official center coordinate for a precise track. 50+ inch extreme rainfall totals are event-wide and occurred over later days, not at landfall.

cases.title: Lake Okeechobee storm surge overtops levees during the 1928 hurricane
cases.location: Lake Okeechobee communities in south Florida
cases.source_publisher: Association of State Dam Safety Officials
cases.primary_angle: Explain how wind setup across shallow Lake Okeechobee combined with wave runup to overtop and erode inadequate flood defenses during September 16–17.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare the storm's coastal landfall on the evening of September 16 to the lake flooding that followed overnight, using original lake-stage and levee-layout records.
cases.verified_core_fact: The 1928 hurricane struck southeast Florida on September 16 and caused deadly overtopping and levee breaches at Lake Okeechobee during the September 16–17 event.
cases.graphic_type: Cross-section of wind setup and levee overtopping
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Technical case explains wind setup, runup and levee erosion; build an original conceptual cross-section and distinguish historic levee geometry from later engineering reconstruction.
cases.research_note: September 17 is an overnight continuation of the September 16 evening landfall, NOT the coastal landfall date. Fatality estimates differ widely with revisions and undercounting of Black migrant workers; no figure cleared. Avoid copying damfailures.org schematics or historic photographs without checking asset rights. The Sep18 calendar primary concerns the separate 1926 Miami hurricane.

cases.title: Tropical Storm Ophelia makes landfall near Emerald Isle, North Carolina
cases.location: Emerald Isle and Pamlico Sound region, North Carolina
cases.source_publisher: North Carolina Department of Public Safety
cases.primary_angle: Explain how a coastal low organized into a high-end tropical storm and drove water into North Carolina's vulnerable estuaries.
cases.alternate_angle: Contrast official estimated sustained winds at landfall against sampled offshore and onshore gusts, then map localized soundside surge impacts.
cases.verified_core_fact: Ophelia made landfall near Emerald Isle, North Carolina on the morning of September 23, 2023 as a tropical storm.
cases.graphic_type: Soundside surge and coastal wind-observation map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NHC cyclone chronology, NWS regional station time series and NC emergency management flooded-community reports; asset rights remain unreviewed.
cases.research_note: NC DPS places landfall near 6:15 a.m. EDT with estimated sustained winds 70 mph; NHC update at 6:20 a.m. confirms landfall. Do not equate offshore gusts with mainland sustained wind. High tide, wind-driven water and rainfall flooding can overlap; avoid assigning each impact without provenance.

cases.title: Hurricane Nate makes its first Gulf Coast landfall at the Mississippi River mouth
cases.primary_angle: Show how an unusually fast-moving hurricane crossed the central Gulf before its first landfall at the river mouth.
cases.alternate_angle: Distinguish the October 7 Mississippi River mouth landfall from the later overnight second landfall near Biloxi, Mississippi.
cases.verified_core_fact: Hurricane Nate made its first landfall near the mouth of the Mississippi River on October 7, 2017 during the evening local time.
cases.graphic_type: Two-landfall coastal-track schematic
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NHC advisory/archive track and NWS Mobile radar; create an original track with local/UTC annotations; NOAA charts are source data, not generic clearance for all webpage images.
cases.research_note: NHC issued a 7 p.m. CDT landfall update. The Biloxi-area second landfall occurred after local midnight on October 8; different UTC times may alter calendar categorization. Two NOAA offices do not establish independent underlying evidence. Avoid copying media storm imagery without item-level rights.

cases.title: Hurricane Zeta accelerates into southeastern Louisiana
cases.primary_angle: Show the combination of late Gulf intensification and fast northeastward translation that carried destructive winds far inland.
cases.alternate_angle: Separate operational landfall intensity, later NHC reanalysis, and direct near-surface observations around Cocodrie and New Orleans.
cases.verified_core_fact: Hurricane Zeta made landfall along the southeastern Louisiana coast near Cocodrie on the afternoon of October 28, 2020.
cases.graphic_type: Original cyclone track, radar and forward-speed plot
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NHC advisories, NWS NOLA radar archive and official track permit an original timeline; reconcile post-analysis intensity and local/UTC timing; image rights unreviewed.
cases.research_note: The operational NHC bulletin reported Zeta making landfall at 4 p.m. CDT (21 UTC), while later NHC reanalysis may place peak category differently. Do not quote 110/115 mph or Cat2/Cat3 without final TCR scope. Avoid implying storm was slow because impacts stretched to Alabama. December 2017 Skirball fire and other candidate categories help counter tropical repetition.

cases.title: A severe tropical cyclone makes landfall in Bangladesh
cases.location: Bangladesh coast and northern Bay of Bengal
cases.source_publisher: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization
cases.secondary_source_publisher: NOAA Atlantic Oceanographic and Meteorological Laboratory
cases.primary_angle: Explain how high cyclone winds and storm surge amplified coastal flood exposure in densely populated delta communities.
cases.alternate_angle: Show the uncertainty in historical cyclone intensity and storm-surge reporting; explain how warning and shelter systems differ from modern Bangladesh practice.
cases.verified_core_fact: A severe tropical cyclone struck Bangladesh on November 29, 1988, producing damaging winds and coastal flooding.
cases.graphic_type: Reconstructed historical cyclone-track and surge-exposure map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Use period-appropriate cyclone reports and coastal elevation data, rather than inferred exact individual loss boundaries or false modern satellite image dating.
cases.research_note: FAO and NOAA AOML give compatible date and broad event but their numerical winds, surge, damage and fatalities draw on legacy reports of inconsistent quality. An old NOAA retrospective describes estimated ~2,000 fatalities; do not use casualty totals without origin and later historical review. Distinguish the cyclone from November 1970 Bhola event already on Nov12.

cases.title: The Skirball Fire erupts above Los Angeles under dry fire-weather conditions
cases.location: Sepulveda Pass and Bel-Air, Los Angeles, California
cases.primary_angle: Show how extreme fire-weather conditions and terrain-aligned winds helped drive December 6 brush-fire spread close to dense development.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain how morning winds, canyon orientation, vegetation and highway adjacency affected incident progression, without confusing ignition cause with fire weather.
cases.verified_core_fact: The Skirball Fire broke out along the Sepulveda Pass corridor of Los Angeles on the morning of December 6, 2017.
cases.graphic_type: Topographic fire progression and wind-direction map
cases.graphic_data_source_note: LAFD timeline and CAL FIRE incident metadata; map roads/terrain independently and obtain exact origin/containment geography before plotting fire progression.
cases.research_note: LAFD logs first response around 4:52 a.m.; CAL FIRE lists 6:31 a.m. as incident start, a metadata discrepancy that must not be presented as two ignition times without context. Fire origin and cause investigations are separate from weather exacerbation. Avoid assuming archival photographs or incident maps are licensed.

cases.title: Russian River crests during California's December 2014 atmospheric river
cases.location: Guerneville, Russian River watershed, northern California
cases.source_publisher: UC San Diego Center for Western Weather and Water Extremes
cases.primary_angle: Connect the December 11 moisture plume and frontal rainband to the December 12 Russian River stage crest, emphasizing rainfall-to-runoff lag.
cases.alternate_angle: Use hourly gauge stage and six-hour IVT timing to show why atmospheric-river intensity does not map one-to-one to river stage.
cases.verified_core_fact: An atmospheric-river storm brought heavy rain and flooding to northern California December 10–12, 2014; USGS deployed crews to monitor high river flows on December 12.
cases.graphic_type: Original rainfall-IVT-river-stage sequence
cases.graphic_data_source_note: CW3E research and USGS measured time-series; a separate peer-reviewed 2021 AMS paper dates the Guerneville crest around 1 p.m. local December 12, but verify gauge datum/time before graphic.
cases.research_note: Northern California's most intense synoptic rain began December 11; December 12 is selected for river-flood follow-through and hydrologic observations. AMS MWR 2021 analysis documents Guerneville stage exceeding flood stage near 1300 local Dec12; no absolute reading is ready for public copy without gauge cross-check. Different response/summary sources do not make the same gauge measurement independent.

cases.title: Rockford reaches an all-time low of −31°F during the 2019 Arctic outbreak
cases.secondary_source_publisher: Illinois State Climatologist / Illinois State Water Survey
cases.primary_angle: Use hourly airport records and a synoptic analysis to explain how snow cover and an intense Arctic high helped northern Illinois reach historic low temperatures.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare Rockford's verified −31°F with Chicago's different-date minimum; explain the difference between air temperature and wind chill.
cases.verified_core_fact: Rockford, Illinois recorded an all-time record low of −31°F on January 31, 2019 during a severe Arctic cold outbreak.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS Rockford temperature record and Illinois State Climatologist month summary; station and observation-day definitions must be preserved.
cases.research_note: Chicago's coldest morning was January 30, not the January 31 Rockford record. NWS and Illinois State Climatologist use common official station readings, not independently observed thermometers. Do not conflate −31°F actual minimum with apparent-temperature wind chill. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-5229075. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-867918, ncei-615345.
cases.graphic_type: Original station minimum-temperature comparison

cases.title: Record flooding overwhelms Rhode Island as March rains continue
cases.location: Cranston, Warwick and Pawtuxet River basin, Rhode Island
cases.source_publisher: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management
cases.primary_angle: Explain antecedent March rainfall and near-saturated watersheds leading to historic flooding, with separate dates for rising stage and the later river crest.
cases.alternate_angle: Show how river gauge hydrographs differed from March 30 impacts to the March 31 crest at Cranston.
cases.verified_core_fact: A severe late-March rainstorm produced major flooding across Rhode Island on March 30–31, 2010 after weeks of unusually wet weather.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Pawtuxet River station time series and record stage reviews; verify gauge datum and do not label March 31 crest as March 30.
cases.research_note: The Pawtuxet River at Cranston reached its record crest March 31, not March 30. This day is the expanding flood emergency and heavy rain; 15-inch month accumulation and 20.7-foot crest require station/time checks. NWS and Rhode Island agencies rely on shared USGS stage data. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-5596629. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-159842, ncei-621930.
cases.graphic_type: River-stage hydrograph and rainfall chronology

cases.title: Training thunderstorms flood Chicago and northern Illinois
cases.location: Chicago metro and northern Illinois rivers
cases.primary_angle: Examine how a nearly stationary frontal boundary and a deep moist plume generated prolonged overnight April 17–18 rain.
cases.alternate_angle: Plot documented storm rainfall against river stage without confusing urban flash flooding with later Des Plaines/Illinois River crests.
cases.verified_core_fact: Heavy rain and thunderstorms from late April 17 through April 18, 2013 caused major flash flooding in the Chicago region and northern Illinois.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Use official station rainfall and gauge records with exact 24-hour windows; do not reuse news broadcast photographs or graphics.
cases.research_note: NWS documents 4–8-inch rainfall in worst affected areas across multiday storm, not an all-Chicago or strictly calendar-day total. Some downstream flood peaks occurred later; CBS rainfall reporting is not an independent rain gauge. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-1018335. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-5292030, ncei-825300.
cases.graphic_type: Original rainfall and urban river-network map

cases.title: Deadly floods strike KwaZulu-Natal as heavy rain persists
cases.location: Durban, KwaZulu-Natal and eastern South Africa
cases.source_publisher: South African Government / KwaZulu-Natal Disaster Management
cases.secondary_source_publisher: South African Weather Service coverage via East Coast Radio
cases.primary_angle: Explain how persistent coastal rain and steep terrain contributed to flood and slope instability around Durban.
cases.alternate_angle: Map rainfall observation areas and landslide/flood impacts without equating preliminary emergency calls with confirmed storm totals.
cases.verified_core_fact: Extremely heavy rain and flooding affected KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa by April 23, 2019, with emergency response ongoing.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Locate SAWS verified rainfall records and local terrain; archived disaster photos remain subject to their actual licenses.
cases.research_note: Government April 23 briefing describes overnight emergencies and continued rainfall. Casualty figures varied with early reporting, so no numeric impact totals are publication-cleared. East Coast Radio quotes SAWS, not a second independent rainfall observation. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-5643351. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-5497063, ncei-1011588.
cases.graphic_type: Topographic rainfall and flood/landslide context map

cases.title: Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm Mocha strikes western Myanmar
cases.primary_angle: Explain cyclone structure, approach angle and coastal exposure during the May 14 Rakhine landfall, separating storm-surge forecasts from measured inundation.
cases.alternate_angle: Reconstruct wind and coastal surge hazards with dated RSMC advisories and distinct humanitarian field reports.
cases.verified_core_fact: Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm Mocha made landfall on Myanmar's Rakhine coast near Sittwe on May 14, 2023.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Use RSMC New Delhi advisories or best track and original coastline vectors; specific UN photographs or satellite products need item-level licensing.
cases.research_note: WMO quotes RSMC New Delhi wind estimates; UN situation report gives approximate local crossing time around 12:30. Do not treat forecast 2–2.5 m surge as a measured water level, and do not reuse evolving disaster figures as final. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-962404. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-10324725, ncei-10316827.
cases.graphic_type: Best-track cyclone center and coastal hazard map

cases.title: A rain-wrapped EF4 tornado crosses the Lawrence–Linwood corridor
cases.primary_angle: Use verified damage surveys to explain why a rain-wrapped, wide tornado posed unusual situational-awareness challenges.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare radar velocity and KU structural damage observations without equating EF intensity to a directly measured surface wind.
cases.verified_core_fact: An EF4 tornado tracked through the Lawrence–Linwood area of Kansas on May 28, 2019.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS path and KU post-storm engineering survey can inform a new map; field photographs are separately owned and not cleared.
cases.research_note: NWS notes EF3 damage near Lawrence and EF4 in Leavenworth County; do not claim EF4 damage throughout. The already selected May 27 and May 29 dates are also tornado stories; flag three-day tornado streak for editorial rebalancing. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-691694. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-237216, ncei-898115.
cases.graphic_type: Original tornado-path map plus documented structural damage intensity

cases.title: Hurricane Agnes crosses the Florida Panhandle before its historic flood track
cases.location: Florida Panhandle, later U.S. East Coast and Mid-Atlantic
cases.secondary_source_publisher: NOAA National Hurricane Center historical review
cases.primary_angle: Explain how a near-minimal hurricane evolved into an enormous inland flood episode after its June 19 Florida landfall and interaction with midlatitude dynamics.
cases.alternate_angle: Contrast coastal wind/surge impacts with later Pennsylvania and New York freshwater rainfall; timeline must distinguish storm phases.
cases.verified_core_fact: Hurricane Agnes crossed the Florida Panhandle coast on June 19, 1972 before its remnants caused far-reaching floods farther north.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: USGS precipitation/flood studies and NHC best-track points, clearly dated; rights and underlying storm analysis verified separately.
cases.research_note: Most extreme Mid-Atlantic flood impacts occurred days AFTER Florida landfall. NHC calls Agnes barely a hurricane in Florida; never attribute later flood deaths or totals to the single June 19 date. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-644664. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-43944, ncei-1176670.
cases.graphic_type: Track and time-stamped rainfall/synoptic transition

cases.title: Seoul faces severe flooding after extraordinary overnight rainfall
cases.primary_angle: Compare rain gauge time windows and the extreme urban drainage response, distinguishing a measured August 8 daily total from August 9 flooding.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain how a stalling frontal boundary produced intense, persistent convective rain over a densely built city.
cases.verified_core_fact: Severe flooding and emergency response continued across Seoul on August 9, 2022 after exceptionally heavy rainfall began August 8.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Only use authentic KMA or municipal observations with proper date/time windows; Yonhap photographs require licensing.
cases.research_note: Two dated Yonhap accounts are NOT independent institutions; the most extreme Dongjak station calendar-day total (381.5 mm) was measured August 8, not August 9. Require an independent KMA or city government dataset and resolve AWS-versus-official-station record comparisons before claim-level approval. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-526593. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-10331334, ncei-1290166.
cases.graphic_type: Seoul basin rainfall and subway disruption schematic

cases.title: Wildfire threat brings evacuation alerts to parts of Yellowknife
cases.primary_angle: Show wildfire progression and forecast wind evolution preceding Yellowknife's partial evacuation alerts.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain the difference between an evacuation alert, the territory's state of emergency on August 15, and the broader evacuation order on August 16.
cases.verified_core_fact: On August 15, 2023, parts of western Yellowknife were placed under wildfire evacuation alert as the Northwest Territories emergency intensified.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Use official dated evacuation alert area and satellite hotspot perimeters, not later full evacuation boundaries.
cases.research_note: Do NOT say all Yellowknife was ordered evacuated on August 15: citywide evacuation order followed on August 16. The GNWT public bulletin did not render fully in browser, but its search excerpt and contemporary Cabin Radio account identify specific neighborhoods. Full primary alert text must be manually rechecked. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-643399. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-1053665, ncei-1136321.
cases.graphic_type: Dated fire perimeter and alert zone map

cases.title: Dallas–Fort Worth is hit by extraordinary overnight flash flooding
cases.location: Dallas and Fort Worth, North Texas
cases.primary_angle: Examine how a nearly stationary upper trough and tropical moisture feed produced intense overnight urban rain and rapid flooding.
cases.alternate_angle: Map observed 24-hour rainfall to urban and creek-gauge response, distinguishing any individual 15-inch spot maximum from a city-wide total.
cases.verified_core_fact: Severe flash flooding affected the Dallas–Fort Worth region August 21–22, 2022, with major impacts and emergency response on August 22.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NCEI Storm Events narrative and NWS station/gauge histories; reconstruct data from timestamps before adding exact rainfall bins.
cases.research_note: Original NCEI catalog supplies segment records; account is now a regional event story rather than a single county event. Highest rainfall values vary by gauges and periods; do not call >15 inches universal. Nearby Aug 23 story is a DIFFERENT 1998 Texas flood from remnant Charley. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-1290020. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-243588, ncei-328830.
cases.graphic_type: Hourly rainfall and watershed runoff map

cases.title: Imelda triggers catastrophic flash flooding in southeast Texas
cases.primary_angle: Analyze the near-stationary inland tropical remnant, extreme moisture, and multiple short-duration rainfall maxima that prompted flash flood emergencies.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare 12/24/48-hour precipitation windows and where localized catastrophic floods differed from Imelda's landfall site on September 17.
cases.verified_core_fact: Remnants of Tropical Storm Imelda produced destructive flash flooding across southeast Texas on September 19, 2019.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS Lake Charles radar precipitation and published AEP windows; original plots require validation of gauges and period bounds.
cases.research_note: Imelda made landfall on September 17, NOT September 19. WWA examines September 19–20 rainfall with independent attribution modeling but relies partly on NOAA rain data. Early fatality/property estimates not cleared; 1-in-1200 year station statistical probability is NOT a universal literal return interval. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-262703. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-406779, ncei-858116.

cases.title: Tasmania records its wettest October day as major flooding develops
cases.location: Northern Tasmania and Mersey–Meander basins, Australia
cases.primary_angle: Explain how a slow-moving frontal rainband connected to tropical moisture dumped record 24-hour rain on saturated Tasmanian catchments.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare the 24 hours ending 9 a.m. October 14 rainfall with subsequent river crest timing and evacuation warnings.
cases.verified_core_fact: In the 24 hours to 9 a.m. October 14, 2022, Tasmania recorded its wettest October day statewide and widespread major flood warnings.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: BoM lists Mount Barrow 188.8 mm in the 24 hours to 9 a.m. on Oct 14, plus other records; dataset time-zone and end-time need accurate caption.
cases.research_note: Meteorological daily rain is the 24h ending at 9 a.m. local, including rain on October 13. Do not attribute full multiday floods to the October 14 calendar day. BoM historical maps need asset-level reuse checks. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-923474. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-5716956, ncei-980123.

cases.title: Tropical Storm Sandy forms in the southwest Caribbean
cases.location: Southwestern Caribbean Sea south of Jamaica
cases.source_publisher: NOAA National Hurricane Center historical advisory
cases.secondary_source_publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada hurricane season review
cases.primary_angle: Use the actual first advisories to show how a nascent October Caribbean tropical storm later developed a large wind field through multiple atmospheric interactions.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare initial Oct 22 tropical formation south of Jamaica to post-tropical evolution much later without implying U.S. impacts happened that day.
cases.verified_core_fact: Sandy reached tropical-storm intensity in the southwestern Caribbean on October 22, 2012.

cases.title: Wildfire smoke blankets San Diego in a satellite-visible plume
cases.location: San Diego County and southern California
cases.primary_angle: Explain how October 27 smoke plumes and Santa Ana flow transformed a wildfire emergency into an exceptional regional air-quality crisis.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare NASA's precisely dated Oct27 Aqua MODIS plume with verified October 27 PM2.5 filter measurements in San Diego County.
cases.verified_core_fact: On October 27, 2003, a NASA Aqua satellite image showed immense wildfire smoke plumes from the Cedar, Paradise and Otay fires blanketing the San Diego region.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NASA Aqua MODIS on 27 October is date-specific; image may have NASA public-domain terms but must check this asset and its credits explicitly.
cases.research_note: Cedar and other fires ignited October 25–26, not October 27. Air Pollution Research paper reports Chula Vista PM2.5 24-hour filter maximum around 240 µg/m³ on Oct27; assess instrument records and whether a regional 24-h filter measurement can be compared with instantaneous satellite plume. No satellite media rights cleared. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-199043. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-855017, ncei-480568.

cases.title: Post-tropical Noel enters Atlantic Canada's warning region
cases.location: Atlantic Canada offshore waters and Maritime provinces
cases.source_publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada / Canadian Hurricane Centre
cases.secondary_source_publisher: NOAA National Hurricane Center season narrative
cases.primary_angle: Explain how Noel's transition from a tropical cyclone into an expansive extratropical gale altered the distribution of wind, rain and heavy seas.
cases.alternate_angle: Use a 0000 UTC November 3 transformation timeline and Canadian warning zones without describing the November 4 Nova Scotia landfall as a November 3 event.
cases.verified_core_fact: By the morning of November 3, 2007, Noel had become a large post-tropical storm and entered the Canadian Hurricane Centre response zone.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: ECCC Canada archives and NHC post-analysis; plot track from authentic coordinates, carefully noting UTC/day boundaries.
cases.research_note: NHC says extratropical transition was at 0000 UTC Nov 3. Subsequent Nova Scotia landfall was just AFTER 0600 UTC on Nov 4; do not call Nov3 a landfall day. Canadian archive is distinct from NHC but uses common storm-track data. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-1225079. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-346665, ncei-67789.
cases.graphic_type: Extratropical transition and expanding wind-field timeline

cases.title: Former Hurricane Eta's flooding worsens across Honduras
cases.source_publisher: NOAA National Hurricane Center / Weather Prediction Center
cases.secondary_source_publisher: United Nations in Honduras situation assessment
cases.primary_angle: Show how Eta's movement across Central American mountains and persistent moisture feed generated dangerous flooding long after coastal landfall.
cases.alternate_angle: Combine dated November 5 advisory center locations and later verified humanitarian flood footprints, avoiding final-loss estimates in early reports.
cases.verified_core_fact: On November 5, 2020, Tropical Depression Eta remained over northern Honduras while the region endured significant flooding from the multiday cyclone.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NHC dated Nov5 advisory and UN November7 situation narrative; any mapped rainfall/landslide grids must be independently checked and image rights reviewed.
cases.research_note: Eta made initial Nicaragua landfall on November 3 and caused multiday regional rainfall and landslides. November 5 is a Honduras flooding/remnant-circulation stage, not first landfall. UN assessment published November 7 summarizes prior impacts, not an independent November 5 meteorological observation. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-863855. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-1148655, ncei-727471.
cases.graphic_type: Terrain, remnant center track and rainfall/landslide-hazard context

cases.title: Storm Bert sweeps Ireland with widespread heavy rain and storm-force winds
cases.location: Ireland, including Mayo, Galway and Cork
cases.primary_angle: Explain the sharp warm-frontal transition from pre-storm cold/snow into strong Atlantic winds and heavy rain.
cases.alternate_angle: Contrast an authentic Nov23 Irish surface analysis with official 24-hour rain and station gust measurements, distinguishing daily totals and storm-wide accumulations.
cases.verified_core_fact: Storm Bert brought widespread heavy rain and damaging winds to Ireland on Saturday, November 23, 2024.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Met Éireann November climate statement includes 12 UTC 23 Nov surface analysis; UK Met Office covers later UK impacts. Exact imagery license/third-party overlays must be reviewed.
cases.research_note: The UK Met Office retrospective describes UK storm impacts and overlaps the same cyclone, but does not independently verify an individual Irish station report. Met Éireann's later review gives 57.4 mm at Knock Airport Nov23; a recorded station total is not all-Ireland precipitation. Storm Bert continued through Nov25. Displaced primary preserved: ncei-1219854. Previously selected alternate IDs retained, not independently researched: ncei-1143746, ncei-143311.
